questions.question: People working on a disabled vehicle:

options.text: Are probably aware of the roadway.
May focus on repairs and not notice traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: May focus on repairs and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people fixing a disabled vehicle on the roadside. They may be focused on the repair work and not paying attention to traffic.

questions.question: Which of the following is not tie-down equipment?
questions.correctAnswerText: Velcro
questions.explanation: You must use the right amount of tie-downs to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer. Tie-down equipment includes ropes, straps, and chains.

questions.question: Vehicles driving behind a truck:

options.text: May have difficulty seeing objects in front of the truck.
Often have a great view of the roadway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have difficulty seeing objects in front of the truck.
questions.explanation: Your truck can block the view of drivers behind you. They may not see hazards that make you need to stop. Flash your brakes and warn other drivers before slowing or stopping.

questions.question: If the ABS light comes on while driving, it means:

options.text: The ABS cannot work due to weather.
The ABS has just been activated.
The ABS is not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: An ABS warning light means there is a problem with the Anti-Lock Braking System that needs to be fixed.

questions.question: You must have an air brake endorsement:

options.text: To use a vehicle with air brakes.
To drive any truck with a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To use a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes knowledge test to get a license to operate vehicles with air brakes, including air over hydraulic braking systems.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe level, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: If the coolant temperature gauge goes too high, stop driving as soon as possible. There may be a problem that could cause engine failure or fire.

questions.question: Drowsy driving happens most often during:
questions.correctAnswerText: The night.
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is most common at night because people are naturally less alert when they normally sleep. Take precautions to prevent fatigue if you must drive at night.

questions.question: You should check and adjust your mirrors:
questions.correctAnswerText: Before driving.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before you start driving. Your posture changes day to day, and your mirrors may need adjustment.

questions.question: Escape ramps are used to:

options.text: Allow only automobiles to exit, not trucks.
Leave the highway and enter a two-lane road.
Stop runaway vehicles on steep downhills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop runaway vehicles on steep downhills.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep downhill slopes to safely stop runaway vehicles. They are made of loose, soft material and sometimes have an uphill slope.

questions.question: Steering wheel play should be no more than:
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 degrees.
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play. This is about two inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel. Too much play makes steering difficult.

questions.question: What color light shows that anti-lock brakes are not working?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Vehicles with anti-lock braking systems have yellow warning lights. These lights indicate a problem with the braking system.

questions.question: When checking your mirrors, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the passenger side mirror
Do not use the driver's side mirror
Use mirrors on both sides of the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Use mirrors on both sides of the vehicle
questions.explanation: Check mirrors on both sides of your vehicle while driving. This helps you see what is happening behind and to the sides of your vehicle.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Stay a safe distance away from the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay a safe distance away from the vehicle
questions.explanation: Give a distracted driver plenty of space. Keep a safe distance behind them.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: As you go down the hill and gain speed
Before you start going down the hill

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start going down the hill
questions.explanation: Slow down and shift into a lower gear before you start down a hill. If you go too fast down a hill, your brakes can overheat and stop working.

questions.question: When you need to back up, what should you do first?

options.text: Drive backward as fast as possible
Walk the path to look for obstacles
Use only the passenger side mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk the path to look for obstacles
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out and walk the area to check for obstacles. Drive slowly while checking both mirrors.

questions.question: What gear-changing method do most heavy vehicles use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Double clutching
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching to change gears.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, how far ahead should you watch the road?
questions.correctAnswerText: A quarter mile
questions.explanation: Watch the road 12 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. At highway speeds, this is about a quarter mile.

questions.question: When driving a truck that requires a CDL, must you wear a seat belt?

options.text: No, you do not need to wear a seat belt
Only if you are carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo
Yes, you must always wear a seat belt

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you must always wear a seat belt
questions.explanation: You must wear a safety belt at all times when driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: In wet conditions, if you see no spray from other vehicles' tires, what does this mean?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road
The spray is stuck under the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road
questions.explanation: No tire spray in wet conditions means ice has formed on the road. Be very careful when driving in wet, freezing weather.

questions.question: When backing up a truck, what should you do first?

options.text: Use your mirrors to guide you
Walk the area to look for obstacles

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk the area to look for obstacles
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around your vehicle to check the path and look for obstacles. Mirrors have blind spots, so do not rely on them alone. Ask a helper to guide you if possible.

questions.question: What endorsement do you need to transport hazardous materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazardous materials
questions.explanation: You need a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials.

questions.question: What happens when you start a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS)?

options.text: The ABS indicator light turns on, then quickly turns off.
The steering wheel will not move until the air tanks are full.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS indicator light turns on, then quickly turns off.
questions.explanation: When you start a vehicle with ABS, the indicator light should come on and then turn off. If the light stays on, there is a problem with the ABS.

questions.question: Can talking on a hands-free phone while driving be distracting?

options.text: No, it does not distract the driver.
Only if the driver is speaking.
Yes, it can distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can distract the driver.
questions.explanation: Hands-free phones are safer than hand-held phones, but they still distract drivers. Talking takes your mental focus away from driving.

questions.question: Why is traction important for driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: Safe braking.
questions.explanation: You cannot brake or steer without traction. Check your tires before you drive.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air has water and oil in it. This can damage the brake system if it builds up. Drain valves remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.question: What must a driver do when exiting a bus?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep contact with the handrail.
questions.explanation: When exiting a bus, you must face the vehicle and keep contact with the handrail at all times. Not doing this correctly can result in failing the test.

questions.question: What do ABS brakes do?

options.text: Help prevent the wheels from locking up.
Stop the vehicle from speeding uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help prevent the wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS) stop the wheels from locking when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: How should you do an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What is important when loading a trailer?

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Balance the weight evenly over the axles.
Put weight only over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Balance the weight evenly over the axles.
questions.explanation: Load must be balanced properly. Too much weight on an axle damages it and makes steering harder. Too little weight causes poor traction and handling problems.

questions.question: What does gravity do on an uphill grade?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow your vehicle down.
questions.explanation: Gravity slows your vehicle on uphill grades. You may need to shift to a lower gear for steep grades.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Have heaters to prevent them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces. Drive carefully on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: When a vehicle is started, the coolant temperature should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slowly.
questions.explanation: After an engine starts, the coolant temperature should rise gradually until it reaches the normal operating temperature.

questions.question: Reading a text message while driving is:

options.text: Allowed only if you are not pulling a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal.
questions.explanation: Sending and reading text messages while driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of when to change gears?

options.text: The speed of the vehicle next to you

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of the vehicle next to you
questions.explanation: There are two signs for when to shift gears. First is engine speed (rpm). Check your manual for the correct rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. Second is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear, then watch your speedometer and shift up as needed. Other drivers' speeds do not matter.

questions.question: A person driving with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.text: A person who is dressed inappropriately.
A person who likes fresh air.

questions.correctAnswerText: A distracted driver.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs that other drivers may be impaired. Drivers who are drunk, sleepy, on drugs, or sick create hazards. One sign of an impaired driver is windows rolled down in cold weather.

questions.question: When slowing down, you should ____ to warn other drivers.
questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes
questions.explanation: Before slowing down, lightly tap your brakes. This makes your brake lights flash and warns drivers behind you.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts could be loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check if the nuts are tight when you see rust in this area.

questions.question: On a leaf spring:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leaves should not be broken.
questions.explanation: Check that leaf springs have no missing or broken leaves. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.

questions.question: When driving, being aware of what is happening behind you is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Important.
questions.explanation: When driving, watch what is happening behind and to the sides of your vehicle. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder as part of your regular scanning.

questions.question: Hanging meat:

options.text: Should never be transported by trailer.
Must be approved by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be an unstable load.
questions.explanation: Drive carefully when carrying hanging meat. This load is unstable because it has a high center of gravity and the meat can swing, which affects how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: Where is the tire load rating stated?

options.text: On the side of the tire.
On the inside of the tire.
On the inside of the driver's door.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of the tire.
questions.explanation: The tire load rating shows the maximum safe weight a tire can carry. This information is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: Is rough acceleration recommended when driving?

options.text: It is encouraged at slow speeds.
It is encouraged at all speeds.
It is discouraged at all speeds.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is discouraged at all speeds.
questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle and cause jerking movements.

questions.question: How should cargo inside a trailer be handled?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
It should be stacked no more than three feet high.
It should be secured to prevent movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be secured to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: All cargo in a trailer must be secured properly to stop it from shifting during transport.

questions.question: What helps a driver stay alert while driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: Staying fit and healthy
questions.explanation: Exercise and a healthy diet help you stay alert while driving. Heavy foods and warm temperatures can make you drowsy.

questions.question: How many driver's licenses can a person have?

options.text: Two licenses: one for automobiles and one for trucks.
A license for every state in which they drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only one license.
questions.explanation: A person can have only one license. Breaking this law can result in jail time and/or a fine of up to $5,000.

questions.question: What should you do if being tailgated?

options.text: Increase the space between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: Add more distance between your vehicle and the one ahead. This gives the tailgater room to pass and reduces the need for sudden speed or direction changes.

questions.question: Who is responsible for ensuring cargo is loaded properly?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver must inspect the cargo, check for overloads and poor weight balance, ensure the cargo is secured without blocking their view, and make sure the cargo does not block access to emergency equipment.

questions.question: What is a challenge when transporting hanging meat as cargo?

options.text: It is illegal to transport in most states.
It is always easy to transport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is usually unstable.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable because it has a high center of gravity and the meat swings during transport. This can affect how the driver handles the vehicle.

questions.question: What is a retarder?

options.text: A device that prevents a vehicle from going too fast
A device that prevents a vehicle from being too loud
A device that improves a vehicle's gas mileage

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that prevents a vehicle from going too fast
questions.explanation: A retarder is a device that slows down a vehicle. It helps drivers reduce their use of the brakes.

questions.question: What should you do when passing parked vehicles?

options.text: Watch for signs of a person exiting a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for signs of a person exiting a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked vehicles. A person may step out suddenly without looking for traffic, or a driver may start their vehicle without seeing you coming.
